children.html: Kitbashing is a popular technique in model making and prop building where an individual creates something new by combining parts from multiple existing kits. The term originated in the modeling community but has since been adopted by other groups, such as prop builders and cosplayers, to describe a similar process.

The kitbashing process often involves taking parts from model kits, toys, and other found objects and combining them in unique ways to create something new. This can involve painting, weathering, decals, and other surface customizations as well as cutting, filing, and otherwise modifying the parts to fit together. Kitbashing is often used to refer to the creation of custom sci-fi and fantasy models meant for play or display, but the approach can also be used for more practical purposes, such as creating new tools or modifying existing ones.

blocks.html: The term “kitbashing” is also used in the 3D computer graphics community to describe an analogous process of working from and combining various 3D models or parts, and even recently been adopted as an approach to pixel art through tools like PixelBasher. It should be noted, however, that while physical kitbashing is typically seen as a hobby activity distinct from “modeling”, the practice of working from pre-existing base parts is much more commonplace in standard professional digital art settings, with the use of asset packs or elements from previous games for example, being near universal.

Kitbashing as we know it is distinct from other forms of creation as it relies upon pre-existing consumer products which can be worked upon. Though it has been around for decades now, it has become even more popular in recent years thanks to the internet and social media. Online communities have formed around the practice, allowing people from all over the world to come together and share their creations and techniques. Kitbashing has become a way for artists and makers to express their creativity and push the boundaries of what is possible with existing materials.
